suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding should end with a verified receipt, not a congratulatory message
A read-only first contribution makes onboarding possible without repository write access
Fork setup instructions should distinguish upstream configuration from local agent settings
Expired authentication deserves its own SDK example with an actionable error
Issue templates should show rejected payloads alongside valid submissions
A shared contract test can keep Python and JavaScript SDK behavior aligned
Documentation examples should run unchanged inside a temporary checkout
Retrying an agent submission must not create duplicate work
Review atomic state writes by interrupting them at each filesystem operation
A minimal reproduction beats a screenshot of an agent failure
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to publish a reusable onboarding checklist
Turn repeated review comments into executable checks that contributors can run locally
Two SDK maintainers can share fixtures without sharing implementation choices
A contribution map should connect workshop tasks to observable acceptance criteria
Publish a troubleshooting cookbook built from reproducible failures and verified repairs
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
